theme: The new creation; the New Jerusalem; the river of life
readingInstruction: Read Revelation 21:1-22:5. This is the climax of the whole Bible: the new heavens and new earth, the New Jerusalem, and the river and tree of life. Read slowly. As you read, think back to the first chapters of Genesis, and notice how many things in the Garden of Eden return here.
settingTheScene: The book of Revelation ends with the vision for which the whole Bible has been preparing: God dwelling with his people in a renewed creation. The images are drawn from Isaiah 65-66, Ezekiel 40-48, and Zechariah, and from Genesis 1-3. Where Genesis began with a garden and a marriage, Revelation ends with a city and a marriage. What was lost in the fall is restored and surpassed. This is the goal of the covenants: God with his people. It is why the memory verse for this unit comes from this passage.
observation: “Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more” (21:1).
“Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God” (21:3).
“He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more” (21:4).
“Behold, I am making all things new” (21:5).
“The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations” (22:2).
“No longer will there be anything accursed” (22:3).
“They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads” (22:4).
interpretation:
John sees “a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.” The sea, a symbol of chaos and separation, is gone. Then he sees “the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” The city is the people of God, and the image of the bride unites the two. Then the voice from the throne: “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God.” This is the covenant promise, repeated throughout the Old Testament (Leviticus 26:11-12; Ezekiel 37:27): “I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” The tabernacle and temple were pointers; here the reality has arrived. “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away.” The curse of Genesis 3 is undone.

The one on the throne speaks for the second time in the book: “Behold, I am making all things new.” Not “I am making new things,” but all things new. It is a renewal of creation. “I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the thirsty I will give from the spring of the water of life without payment.” Those who conquer will inherit these things, “and I will be his God and he will be my son.” But the cowardly, faithless, detestable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars will have their portion in the lake of fire. The vision does not hide the stakes.

An angel shows John the Bride, the wife of the Lamb: the holy city, with the glory of God, radiant like a jewel. It has a great high wall with twelve gates, with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and twelve foundations with the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. Old and new covenant people are united. The city is a perfect cube (12,000 stadia each way), like the Most Holy Place in the temple. The whole city is a holy of holies. The wall is jasper, the city pure gold, clear as glass, and the foundations are adorned with every kind of jewel. The gates are pearls, and the street is pure gold. “And I saw no temple in the city, for its temple is the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb.” “And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and its lamp is the Lamb.” The nations walk by its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it. Its gates are never shut, for there is no night. “But nothing unclean will ever enter it… but only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life.”

Chapter 22 returns to Eden. “Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb through the middle of the street of the city; also, on either side of the river, the tree of life with its twelve kinds of fruit, yielding its fruit each month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. No longer will there be anything accursed, but the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will worship him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. And night will be no more. They will need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light, and they will reign forever and ever.” The tree of life, lost in Genesis 3, is restored. The river of Eden, now from the throne. And the greatest promise: “They will see his face.” This is the beatific vision, which no one could have and live (Exodus 33:20). Because of Christ, we will see God’s face, and we will reign with him.
connection: Genesis 1:1-2:25 and 3:22-24 are the beginning that Revelation completes. Isaiah 65:17-25 and 66:22 promise new heavens and a new earth. Ezekiel 37:26-28 and 47:1-12 describe God dwelling with his people and a river from the temple. Leviticus 26:11-12 and 2 Corinthians 6:16 repeat the covenant formula. Isaiah 25:8 and 35:10 promise no more tears. Isaiah 60:1-3, 19-20 pictures nations coming to the light. 1 Kings 6:20 describes the cube-shaped Most Holy Place. Ephesians 2:19-22 and Galatians 4:26 speak of the heavenly Jerusalem. Psalm 17:15 and 1 John 3:2 speak of seeing God. Matthew 5:8 promises the pure in heart will see God.
application:
Read the memory verse (21:3-4) aloud, slowly. Which promise most touches your situation today: no more tears, no more death, no more pain?

Imagine the tree of life and the river. How would knowing that this is where history is headed shape the way you spend the day?

Think of someone who is grieving. Share verse 4 with them, and sit with them.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he will dwell with his people and wipe away every tear.
Tell him what tears you are bringing him.
Ask him to give you hope for the new creation.
